name: Ironwear — The Full Chrome Display Movement
creator: Originating on the Shelf, popularized by performance artist Obinna Szczepańska-Reeves
description: A defiant aesthetic philosophy demanding that all chrome, all ports, all seams, all surgical scarring, and all mechanical augmentation be displayed without covering, polished or weathered according to personal pride. Ironwear began in Shelf communities where replacement parts were salvaged and mismatched — the aesthetic of necessity became a statement of identity. By the 2200s it had been absorbed into Tier 4 luxury fashion, spawning haute couture augment-display lines that cost more than most Shelf residents earn in a decade.
cultural_impact: Ironwear fundamentally altered the corponation augmentation market, driving demand for aesthetically distinctive chrome rather than medically neutral components. It also created one of the sharpest class-friction points in Meridian fashion: the same aesthetic means survival pride on the Shelf and luxury cosplay in the Spire.
controversy: The Spire absorption of Ironwear aesthetics is widely considered the defining example of cultural extraction in GLMZ fashion history. Shelf practitioners coined the phrase 'chrome tourism' to describe Tier 4-5 consumers performing working-class augment culture while paying Φ40,000 for custom designer mismatches.
story_hooks: The original Shelf collective that birthed Ironwear is being evicted from their building — now owned by the luxury fashion house that monetized their aesthetic.
A Spire socialite wearing Ironwear couture is mistaken for a Shelf runner by a corponation security contractor with violent consequences.
Obinna Szczepańska-Reeves resurfaces after a decade of silence to publicly denounce what the movement became — and receives death threats from the fashion houses.
